items.text: Markets: Wall Street is closed for Thanksgiving, so Wednesday is the last save point. The Nasdaq was down as much as 4.6% and clawed back to close down just 0.62%. The Dow even finished up 0.33% at 50,182. Half-day Friday, closing at 1 p.m. ET.
Markets: Bitcoin respawned. It bottomed at $57,500 Wednesday and is holding around $60,800 with stocks closed. Spot bitcoin ETFs still bled $453 million, their seventh straight day of outflows.
Took a Hit: Yesterday's parade-vs-wind matchup is over. Wind won. The 100th Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade is postponed for the first time ever and moves to Saturday at 8:30 a.m.

Happening Now: The nor'easter is playing gatekeeper for Thanksgiving dinner. 360+ U.S. flights canceled and 460+ delayed by late morning, with JFK and Baltimore getting hit hardest. Yesterday, more than 6,000 flights were delayed.

Fixed: Iowa's 5-ton lead azide problem. The Army calls the blast a "huge success," and the EPA says air monitors detected zero airborne lead. Soil and water testing is still underway, so the final verdict is pending.
Took a Hit: The FCC's early license review of ABC. A federal judge blocked it for now, saying the process risks chilling "a broadcaster of ordinary firmness."
Leveling Up: NYC renters. A judge upheld the two-year rent freeze on about 1 million stabilized apartments, a win for Mayor Mamdani. Landlords are not having a happy Thanksgiving.
Leveling Up: North Korea's nuke stockpile, per Kim himself. He left Trump's overture on read and ordered a bigger arsenal, including wider deployment of tactical nukes.
Fixed (barely): Mortgage rates. The 30-year average dipped to 7.21% from 7.28%, which is still close to the 2026 high. Your starter home is still a side quest.

What's New: Yesterday a Treasury official got caught vibe-coding a Civ clone. Today Andrej Karpathy had Claude build a Civilization-style map of the real U.S. from 31 federal data sources. 7 hours, 45K lines of code. Civ is the national pastime now.
Happening Now: The football triple-header is still on, rain or no rain. Bears at Lions at 1 p.m. ET, Eagles at Cowboys at 4:30, and Chiefs at Bills at 8:20 on NBC and Peacock.

What's New: Thanksgiving is officially a shopping holiday with gravy on the side. Adobe forecasts $12.9 billion in online spending on Black Friday, up 9.2%, with Cyber Monday topping out at $15.1 billion.
Took a Hit: Andy Taylor, Duran Duran's original guitarist, died at 65 after a long battle with prostate cancer. Rest easy, legend.
